pageCache.pageTitle: Home | St Amand's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
St Amand's Catholic Primary School
Headteacher's welcome
Our Mission Statement
We work together, play together, pray together and always do our best.We show enthusiasm for our learning.We love one another as Jesus loves us.We look after his world and everything in it.We listen to God and praise him together.
Thank you for taking the time to investigate St Amand's Catholic Primary School. We are a unique school in many ways; in fact we are the only St Amand's school in the country. There is only one chapel dedicated to St Amand in the UK, and that is in Hendred House, close to our school. Our school consists of wonderful children, dedicated, talented staff, committed governors and loyal parents. We are located in a beautiful village with fantastic grounds.
We are extremely proud of our Outstanding Catholic school, recently judged by the Catholic Schools Inspectorate to be outstanding for all areas: CSI Inspection Report (May 2023).pdf.
"St Amand’s has an outstanding Catholic identity. A strong Catholic witness permeates the entire school, resulting in an evangelical ethos which inspires the whole community."
"Pupils across the school clearly understand what it means to be a member of a Catholic community and fully embrace the school’s mission statement. Their behaviour towards each other and other members of the community demonstrates their understanding that we are all made equal before God and loved by Him."
In an ungraded inspection, December 2024, Ofsted judged the school as having taken effective action to maintain the standards identified at that previous inspection: a good school with outstanding for Personal Development, and Behaviour and Attitudes. The report reflects what it is like to attend our school, "Pupils enjoy being a part of a caring community at St Amand’s Catholic Primary School. They learn to be exceptionally polite, to work hard and to treat others with respect. The education provided at the school helps pupils to develop their character, independence and knowledge of the world. The school helps pupils to become the best version of themselves so that they can approach their next steps with confidence.' ." We have a high quality, diverse curriculum, outstanding behaviour and attitudes, high standards of education, very good teaching and excellent pastoral support.
However we are much more than this; our school is a place where each child can come to know the love of Jesus in their lives, where they are valued and respected for their uniqueness and where each child is nurtured. Our school has a strong commitment to Catholic Social Teaching: "Children regularly raise funds for refugees, the homeless and others in poverty." We pray together and go to Mass together; we celebrate feast days and special days throughout the church's year. We have a lot of fun and laugh together. As our Mission Statement says ' We love one another as Jesus loves us.'
We are a small school with four and a half classes; staff know the children well, children have many opportunities to take part in competitions or represent the school in some way during their time with at St Amand's. Children have a strong sense of identity in our small school.
I am proud to lead St Amand's as the headteacher, with its challenges and many more successes to celebrate. We have a wonderful staff who give over and above of their time, who strive to make learning fun.
If you would like to visit the school and meet our staff and children, please contact the school office to make an appointment and Debbie will be happy to help. office.3855@st-amands.oxon.sch.uk
I look forward to meeting you.

St Amand's Catholic Primary School
Sunrise Breakfast Club and Sunsine After School Club
Sunrise Club is a breakfast club which is open every morning from 8.00am to 8.40am. The breakfast consists of a choice of cereals, toast with various toppings, pancakes, yoghurt and fresh fruit. Water and milk are available to drink. The cost for Sunrise Club is £4.00 per day. (from 01.09.2021). All payments are made via the schools online payment system, www.eduspot.co.uk.
Sunshine Club in an after school club which offers a safe, fun and stimulating environment for the children of St Amand’s Catholic Primary School. We have our own light, airy and spacious room within the school building; it is a great place for the children to make new friends and participate in exciting activities. The club is open form Monday to Thursday, in term time only, and operates from 3.15pm – 5.30pm.
The cost of the sessions are: 3.15pm - 4.30pm - £6.00
3.15pm - 5.30pm - £9.50
Bookings for the club are made through the school office and we offer a very flexible booking system. All payments are made via the schools online payment system, www.eduspot.co.uk .
The club is staffed by Mrs Helen Rackley and Mrs Emma Gibbons all of whom are are known by the children. There is a direct emergency line for Sunshine Club. If you need to contact them please call 07907 104617.
Children begin the session by washing their hands and having a snack and a drink whilst chatting to their friends. Children bring their own snack and drink although water is always available.
Activities are planned termly and children are encourages to take part if they wish too. We also have a large selection of toys and games for them to use. The school fields and play areas are also available to use for outside games etc (weather permitting).
Sunrise Club is a breakfast club which is open daily from 8.00am – 8.40am. The breakfast consists of a choice of cereals, toast with various toppings, pancakes, yoghurt and fresh fruit. Water and milk are available to drink. The cost for Sunrise Club is £4.00 per day. All payments are made via the schools online payment system, www.eduspot.co.uk .
All enquiries should be address to the school office on office.3855@st-amands.oxon.sch.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Eco Club | St Amand's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
St Amand's Catholic Primary School
Eco Club: What We’ve Been Up To This Year
Our Eco Club is made up of a small but enthusiastic group of children from Year 1 to Year 6. The older pupils take great pride in supporting and encouraging the younger members, creating a lovely sense of teamwork and shared purpose.
Caring for Our Grounds
Throughout the year, the children take part in a variety of environmental and sustainability projects around the school and in the village. Recently, they prepared our flower and vegetable beds for spring by clearing weeds and planting daffodil, tulip, and allium bulbs—which are now beginning to peek through the soil.
Sustainable Christmas Creations
In the lead‑up to Christmas, Eco Club focused on creative ways to reduce waste. They transformed old Christmas cards into gift tags, crafted compostable decorations, and made mini wreaths and table arrangements using locally foraged greenery. These beautiful creations brought festive cheer while promoting sustainability.
Book & Toy Swap Initiative
Most recently, the children designed eye‑catching posters to promote our upcoming Book and Toy Swap on 10 February. This event is a fantastic way to share resources and give pre‑loved books and toys a new lease of life.
What’s Next?
Over the coming months, Eco Club will be sowing fruit and vegetables in their garden patch. They also plan to continue caring for the benches around school, ensuring they remain welcoming spaces for everyone.
Apple‑Pressing and Charity Fundraising
In October, we rented an apple press from Sustainable Wantage. The children collected, chopped, crushed and pressed hundreds of locally grown and foraged apples, including those picked at Hendred House.They sold the delicious fresh juice at our Harvest Market and proudly donated the proceeds—an amazing £164—to CAFOD.
The Eco Club went litter picking in the village. They filled two bags of litter and even had time for a picnic lunch in the park.
Book swap on World Book Day - everyone enjoyed taking home a different book.

pageCache.pageTitle: House Captains | St Amand's Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
St Amand's Catholic Primary School
St Teresa of Calcutta
St Josephine Bakhita
The Fairtrade Bake Off
The House Captains led the Red Kites Bake Off. Each of the four teams investigated where to buy Fairtrade ingredients and baked delicious cakes which they sold at the Fairtrade Cafe the next day. They served their parents, parishioners and Governors. They were congratulated for being polite, articulate and sensible. They made £119.50 profit. Some will be reinvested into another event and some donated to CAFOD. They now have the baking bug and aim to be entrepreneurs by reinvesting 50% of the profits in another project to accumulate larger profits.
